title: Decision Calculus is the single runtime action-ranking authority
summary: The constitutional runtime now preserves hard eligibility gates and routes every eligible-action ranking decision through the canonical deterministic Decision Calculus.
what_happened: The runtime contained a legacy scalar action-value authority alongside the newer deterministic Decision Calculus. A surgical integration removed the parallel ranking authority without replacing constitutional gates.
what_we_learned: Constitution determines what is permissible; Decision Calculus determines which permissible action has the highest responsible verified value.
A model or candidate cannot manufacture authority or evidence.
Protected human boundaries must be evaluated before value ranking and cannot be outweighed by benefit.
When legacy runtime fields do not contain a calculus dimension, use a neutral value rather than inventing evidence.
Runtime receipts should name the canonical ranking authority explicitly so authority drift is observable.
why_it_matters: Two competing decision authorities create silent architectural drift. One constitutional gate layer plus one deterministic ranking authority makes runtime behavior auditable, testable, and harder to Goodhart.
what_changed: .naya/runtime/naya_power_kernel.py now delegates eligible-action ranking to SUPERBRAIN.naya_power_decision_calculus.
tools/run_superbrain_local_suite.py makes kernel self-test and calculus integration mandatory.
next_best_action: Prove the real NOTE EVENT → PIS / PRIMARY INTELLIGENCE → RUNNING FEED / STATE PROJECTION → fresh Naya retrieval → behavior change path, then verify one safe authorized continuation and successor torch.
